text:
maria-support: Customer on EU account (ACCT-4821) reports corporate card declined at a Brussels POS while paying an invoice. They say vendor is 'TramTech BV' — we see a 402 from the gateway and the UI shows 'merchant category restricted'. Can payments team take a look?

ashley-payments: Thanks — can you paste the processor response body? Also need the card BIN and exact timestamp.

maria-support: Processor response (redacted):
```json
{
  "status": "decline",
  "decline_code": "MCC_RESTRICTED",
  "mcc": "4121",
  "acquirer_response": "05",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-17T09:25:03Z"
}
```
BIN last6: 123456, tx_ts: 2026-03-17T09:25:03Z

jon-dev: MCC 4121 is in our restricted list for corporate cards in the EU compliance profile — see rule: `block_mcc_eu_high_risk`. I can repro locally with the sandbox card token.

jon-dev: Repro steps:
1) curl -X POST https://payments.redwood.internal/v1/payments -d '{"account":"ACCT-4821","amount":198.45,"card_token":"tok_sandbox_123","merchant_mcc":"4121"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $API"
2) Response: 402 + `{"code":"DECLINE_MCC_BLOCK","reason":"merchant category not allowed for corporate card"}`

patrick-ops: Could be the new threshold rule deployed last week that tightened MCC exceptions for EU accounts. We pushed a config change: `eu_mcc_whitelist_threshold=0` for non-enterprise. That would silently block non-whitelisted vendors.

maria-support: Customer says they had been transacting with TramTech for months. They need this transaction to go through for an urgent invoice. What's the fastest safe workaround?

ashley-payments: Short-term options: 1) Create a one-time merchant allowlist override for ACCT-4821 (admin console) — immediate but audit will flag it. 2) Switch payment method to a personal card / ACH. 3) For persistent fix, request vendor docs for compliance to add them to org allowlist.

maria-support: They want the one-time override. Can payments do the admin override and add an audit note with the invoice number?

ashley-payments: I can do it. Giving command I will run: `POST /admin/accounts/ACCT-4821/overrides` with body `{merchant: "TramTech BV", mcc: "4121", scope: "one_time", reason: "Customer urgent invoice 2026-03-17 #INV-7743"}`. Will attach evidence screenshot.

billing-bot: Automated note: override requested by ashley-payments at 2026-03-17T09:33:12Z — pending approval per policy (requires manager sign-off if amount > 5k).

ashley-payments: Override applied for invoice amount 198.45, flagged as one_time. Customer notified. I >created audit ticket PAY-9982.

customer-liaison: Customer confirms payment succeeded after override. They asked why this started now — wanted explanation to share with AP.

jon-dev: Root cause: config tighten we shipped accidentally included EU accounts before enterprise exemptions were fully populated. I'll open PR to add a fail-safe: warn instead of block when account has history with the merchant.

patrick-ops: +1 on fail-safe. Also let's run a job to surface accounts with >3 successful txs to same MCC in last 90 days before blocking.

maria-support: Thanks team — closing this thread but leaving PAY-9982 open for audit follow-up. :white_check_mark:
